name: Nullform Ghostgrip Infiltration Glove
description:
Featherweight operative gloves in near-black matte polymer-skin, cut close with zero-seam construction at the fingertips. The palm and finger pads are coated in a micro-textured gecko-adhesion compound that clings to glass, brushed metal, and polished concrete without residue. Print-masking is achieved through a continuous electrospun polymer film at the fingertips that conforms to the wearer's ridges without transmitting them.

Thin enough to feel a card-reader's surface contours. The cuff is short and elasticated — fits under sleeves without bulk. No branding visible anywhere on the glove. Sold through unlicensed channels only.
functionality: Gecko-adhesion grip on smooth surfaces. Electrospun fingertip film masks biometric prints. No thermal signature bleed at fingertips. Ultra-low profile under standard sleeves. Leaves no adhesive residue on surfaces.
what_it_says: You go places you aren't supposed to and you don't leave evidence.
story_hooks: A print-masked glove is recovered from a Tier 5 Spire vault breach — the gecko-adhesion pattern on the palm matches a specific Nullform batch traced to a single Circuit district distributor.

Someone is selling Nullform Ghostgrips with a hidden flaw: the print-masking film degrades after 40 minutes of body heat, leaving a perfect impression of the wearer's fingerprints on the last surface touched.
related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Gecko Ascender GA-4

physical_description.visual_profile: Sleek, minimalist operator gloves that disappear under clothing. Near-black with an almost invisible matte finish that suggests professional concealment rather than fashion. The silhouette is tight and anatomical, following the hand's natural contours without excess material. Presents as tactical and purposeful—the kind of glove worn by someone who needs to move unseen.
physical_description.fit: Compression-tight through the palm and fingers, conforming precisely to hand geometry. The cuff sits just above the wrist, elasticated for secure hold under jacket or sleeve without creating visible bunching. Zero slack in the construction—every millimeter accounted for.
physical_description.primary_material: Electrospun polymer-skin composite with micro-textured gecko-adhesion compound on contact surfaces. The fingertip overlay is a breathable electrospun film that masks biometric signatures without reducing tactile sensitivity.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost liquid-like matte finish on the back of hand; microscopically textured grip zones on palms and fingertips that feel adhesive without stickiness. The print-masking film is imperceptibly thin, adding no perceptible texture to the fingertips from the wearer's perspective.
physical_description.color_scheme: Near-black with zero-contrast construction—no accent stitching, no visible seams, no tonal variation. Designed to vanish against dark clothing or in low light.
physical_description.closures: Elasticated cuff with friction-fit closure. No zippers, snaps, or buckles—complete absence of mechanical fasteners that could catch or be detected.
distinctive_features: Gecko-adhesion micro-texture for vertical surface climbing
Electrospun biometric masking film on fingertips
Short elasticated cuff designed for concealment under sleeves
No visible branding or manufacturer marks
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 sub-grade/ungoverned. Unlicensed street manufacture. The sophistication of the tech suggests someone with black-market access, but the distribution model and lack of corpo finish scream underground economy.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street operative, infiltrator, or bypass specialist. The wearer is someone engaged in unauthorized access, surveillance evasion, or theft. Possibly corpo extraction team operating outside official channels. Not for civilian use—this is purpose-built for people who need to leave no trace.
physical_description.condition_typical: Appears pristine on purchase, but the gecko-adhesion compound will show microscopic wear patterns from repeated climbing or surface contact. Over time, the fingertip masking film may show minor delamination at the edges, requiring replacement. Used pairs are nearly impossible to date because the gloves leave no wear signature.
